method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse reconstruction of both inductive definitions and induction principles, branch-by-branch review of tagged operator definitions, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison after the documented OLFOL-005 projection. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Inductive definitions of first-order terms and formulas; notation and defined operators; syntactic identity and concatenation; and induction principles for terms and formulas.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A first-order language determines terms and formulas. Variables and constants are terms, and applying an n-place function to n terms gives a term; nothing else does. Variable-free terms are closed, and constants could equivalently be treated as zero-place functions.
samples.checks: The three formation clauses, limiting clause, closed-term definition and zero-place reformulation remain distinct and complete.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Atomic formulas include selected truth constants, predicate applications and identity formulas. Negation, binary connectives and both quantifiers recursively form formulas, and the limiting clause excludes every other string.
samples.checks: Every tag-conditioned base case, arity, term argument, connective constructor, quantifier constructor and limiting clause is retained with its original formula.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The definitions are inductive: atomic formulas enter at the first stage, later stages apply formation rules to formulas already built, and exactly the expressions eventually produced are formulas.
samples.checks: The infinite-stage explanation, four atomic shapes and exhaustive eventual-construction condition are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Identity is conventionally written infix, its negation has a special abbreviation, and outer parentheses on binary formulas may be omitted. Unlike some texts, this presentation does not require a quantified variable to occur in the quantified formula.
samples.checks: Both equality abbreviations, the outermost-parenthesis convention, all tag branches and the optional occurrence restriction are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every defined truth constant, connective and quantifier expands into the displayed primitive notation. The conditional's disjunctive expansion has its frozen unmatched parenthesis removed under OLFOL-005.
samples.checks: All nine tagged expansion clauses and their nested alternatives remain formula-for-formula exact after the one documented delimiter projection.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Application-specific infix and postfix marks abbreviate indexed predicate and function notation. Syntactic identity compares equal-length symbol strings position by position and can describe concatenated strings and substrings.
samples.checks: The arithmetic and set-theory examples, four official expansions, iff condition, concatenation order and substring consequences are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Inductively generated terms and formulas support corresponding induction principles. A property holds of every term if it holds of variables and constants and is preserved by function application; it holds of every formula if it holds atomically and is preserved by every selected constructor.
samples.checks: The language parameters, property P, all base and closure clauses, term side assumption, exercise reference and every tagged formula constructor are preserved.

source_observations: The target preserves the difference between object-language identity and metalinguistic syntactic identity.
The limiting clauses are retained, so the Marathi definitions do not merely state closure conditions.
OLFOL-005 removes one unmatched closing parenthesis from the frozen disjunctive conditional expansion; its source hash, reader note and QA projection are recorded.
All other formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
Several technical compounds remain explicitly provisional in the terminology ledger.
The section states the induction principles but leaves the term-induction proof as an exercise.
